subject: Re: Encord - Next steps
text:
Thanks Sara and Leo,

Appreciate your time on Friday and the quick follow-up.

Wednesday 10:30 UK works well for our next call. Happy to frame the conversation more clearly by addressing the questions below. Please bear in mind that many of these answers are somewhat circular and will largely depend on economics. The reason is that we currently have a huge amount of video content (+2PB) to work through, growing at about 300TB per week. We can, however, increase the pace of content ingestion rapidly if the economics make sense.

What is the expected number of accounts (admins and annotators)?

This depends on how much content each video annotator can process per unit of time. At present we only have audio annotators and our base case is that we would source video annotators from you.

What is the expected number of images or keyframes per month you’d like to visualise/curate?

We currently have a backlog of more than 2PB of unprocessed, unannotated content. This is growing quickly, and we also have a significant amount of additional content “under management” (i.e. contracted to us on an exclusive basis but not yet ingested into our servers).

Once we work through this backlog and scale our partnership, I think a reasonable assumption is ingesting between 500TB and 1PB of content per week. Again, the limiting factor would be economics rather than our ability to source and sign new content.

Do you require any external annotation services? If so, what is the expected amount of data to be annotated per month?

As above, this will depend on the economics. To give some guardrails, it would be helpful to understand the indicative costs for video annotation at different scales — for example, how many video annotators would be required to process 100TB, 200TB, or 500TB of 4K content per week.

Available to address any questions or comments in the meantime.

Thank you,

Nikolay

subject: Re: Preventing CRM logging
text:
Hi Carl! 
 
 My colleague is currently away, I'll step in to assist you, ensuring there's no delay in addressing your needs. 🙌n them up manually. 
 
 You’re right—this is something other teams have bumped into as well, since HubSpot doesn’t allow native subject-line filtering. The workaround we usually see is to set up rules either in Gmail (before the emails get logged) or inside HubSpot with workflows. 
 
 Most teams do one of the following: 
 - Create a Gmail filter that looks for “lemwarmup” in the subject/body and either skips inbox or prevents those emails from being synced to HubSpot. Since your BDRs use the Gmail integration, this filter kicks in before HubSpot sees the email. 
- Alternatively, inside HubSpot some teams build a workflow that auto-tags or archives emails containing “lemwarmup” so they don’t clog reporting. 
 It's not a native HubSpot feature, but these small rules have worked well for others. I would also suggest double checking with CRM support as they might have a better workaround.
